A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PAPRIKA research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original training and evaluation results, including task success, generalization, curriculum learning, ablations, and qualitative trajectory analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds Gemma-3 experiments, single task group controls, additional metrics, and starting-model analyses.

M1.justification: The described self-generated trajectory collection, filtering, SFT followed by RPO, action-token optimization, and coefficient-of-variation/UCB curriculum remain unchanged. Corrected equation signs and applying the pipeline to Gemma do not establish a changed training procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ten task groups, LMRL-Gym evaluations, modified Wordle scenarios, standard-bandit test, and six standard benchmarks. The additional model configurations and controls operate within retained task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds PAPRIKA trained on a single task group to the generalization comparisons in Figures 3 and 13, providing an important task-specific comparator absent from v1. It also adds comparisons with unmodified Gemma-3-12B-IT. GPT-4o-mini and WildChat fine-tuning additionally enter the best-arm-selection comparison in Figures 5–6.

E3.justification: v3 adds Gemma-3-12B-IT experiments and single task group training controls, reports pass@k for k=1–4, and removes the best-of-four turn-count metric. Table 1 also revises the twenty-questions training count from 1,500 to 1,499; this reported correction does not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Generalization analysis expands from five displayed task groups to all ten and adds single-group versus joint training controls. The SFT/RPO ablation expands from four groups to six, adding Minesweeper and Wordle. Appendix I.11 adds starting-model comparisons and observations about unsuccessful DeepSeek-R1 distilled-model inference.

E5.justification: v1 Figures 2 and 5 explicitly identify their bands as standard errors over three seeds. Their expanded counterparts in v3 Figures 6–7 retain bands without that explicit caption information, while the new main summary uses bars without uncertainty indicators. Three-seed reporting remains elsewhere; no increased run count or new statistical procedure is documented.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive Gemma, pass@k, single-group training, and expanded ablation results. Figure 3 reports LOO improvement on nine of ten groups and joint training outperforming single-group training on seven. The best-of-four turn-count results disappear. These additions coexist with unchanged standard-benchmark values in Table 2.

T1.justification: v3 adds the missing leading minus signs to the SFT and DPO loss equations in Section 3.3, correcting their mathematical loss formulation. The POMDP framework, curriculum definitions, and coefficient-of-variation estimator remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof appears.

C1.justification: The abstract and concluding contribution statements retain the same central claims: synthetic interaction training develops transferable decision-making abilities, and curriculum sampling improves data efficiency. Additional experiments support these claims without redefining the core contribution.

C2.justification: v3 clarifies task-directed curiosity and amortized exploration, explicitly identifies Wordle as a case of absent or negative transfer, and discusses limitations associated with lengthy reasoning and starting-model quality. Existing caveats about environment hacking, Minesweeper preference pairs, and limited standard-bandit transfer remain.

D1.justification: New appendices disclose environment/judge temperature and token limits, agent token limits, Gemma training hardware, and explicit code, dataset, and checkpoint access links. These materially expand reproducibility information. The inference settings are newly documented, rather than demonstrated changes to existing experiments; Gemma training-data counts remain unspecified.

R1.justification: The introduction and new Appendix A substantially position PAPRIKA relative to intrinsic motivation and exploration research. Section 5 and Appendix B.2 also expand connections to agent training and text environments, including ReAct, Aviary, TextWorld, and DiscoveryWorld. This extends research positioning beyond isolated citation additions.

P1.justification: Most methodological prose and detailed task prompts remain intact. v3 makes localized introduction and results rewrites, adds explanatory and reproducibility sections, moves WildChat discussion into the appendix, and regroups standard-benchmark details. The principal section sequence remains stable.

P2.justification: Figure 2 changes from six temperature curves to a ten-task bar-chart comparison, and Figure 3 expands its panels and comparator display. Numerous appendix plots are added, recolored, resized, and rearranged; the best-of-four efficiency figure is removed. A new table summarizes initial states, actions, and observations.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens evaluation of the central generality claim through a second model family and direct comparisons with task-specific training, addressing important gaps in v1. Corrected losses, explicit inference settings, and release information also improve reproducibility. Losing the best-of-four efficiency analysis and some explicit uncertainty labeling are limited drawbacks relative to these substantive gains.
